To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
clathrin is required for BL-triggered, asymmetric auxin distribution essential for hypocotl phototropism.
clathrin regulates blue-light-triggered lateral auxion distribution and hypocotyle phototropism.

(1) BL induces the relocalization of CLCs in the hypocotly, (2) CLCs are required for endocytosis of PIN3, (3) CLC-mediated endocytosis is required for BL-triggered lateralization of PINs, (4) CLC-mediated PIN3 endocytosis regulates auxin distribution in a BL-dependent manner and (5) CLC-mediated auxin distribution regulates hypocotyl phototropic bending.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of phototropism, which is an important process for plants to grow towards light for photosynthesis.
the mechanisms by which plants grow toward light, and the role that the hormone auxin and the protein clathrin play in this process.
the molecular mechanisms underlying phototropism, a process that is essential for the survival and development of plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clathrin is required for BL-triggered, auxin-dependent hypocotyl phototropic responses.
CLCs are essential for BL-triggered, asymmetric auxin distribution by regulating the lateral distribution of PINs in hypocotyls.
the clathrin-mediated endocytic pathway is essential for the lateralization of the auxin efflux carrier PIN3, thereby regulating auxin distribution in response to BL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
clathrin is a critical component for BL-triggered, auxin-mediated lateralization of PIN proteins, which is essential for BL-induced phototropic bending.
clathrin-mediated endocytosis is a key regulator of BL-induced lateralization of PIN auxin transporters and thereby auxin distribution in Arabidopsis phototropism.
CLC2 and CLC3 are essential components for BL-triggered, auxin-dependent endocytosis of PIN3 that is critical for asymmetric distribution of auxins and subsequent phototropic bending.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clathrin is required for BL-triggered lateralization of PIN auxin efflux carrier in the hypocotil, thereby regulating auxin distribution and phototropism.
auxin regulates clathrin-mediated endocytic recycling of PIN3 and that this process is essential for BL-triggered asymmetric auxin distribution required for hypocotyl tropic growth in Arabidopsis.
clathrin is a key component in auxin-mediated BL-triggered lateralization of PIN proteins, and thus in hypocotyl tropic bending.
